evals.prompt: Turn this into a skill: every week I export a CSV from our billing system, drop rows where status is refunded, pivot by region, and paste the result into a weekly email. Make me a skill that does it.
evals.expected_output: A new skill directory with a SKILL.md whose description names the artifact produced, and body instructions that generalize beyond the exact columns mentioned.
expectations: A new skill directory with a SKILL.md whose description names the artifact produced, and body instructions that generalize beyond the exact columns mentioned.

evals.prompt: My pdf-tables skill never fires. People ask things like get the numbers out of this report and it just does it by hand instead. Fix the description.
evals.expected_output: A rewritten description that leads with the concrete deliverable and carries at least one negative clause sharing vocabulary with the positives.
expectations: A rewritten description that leads with the concrete deliverable and carries at least one negative clause sharing vocabulary with the positives.

evals.prompt: This SKILL.md is 640 lines and every invocation is paying for all of it. Restructure it so the rarely-needed parts load on demand.
evals.expected_output: Content moved into references/ with pointers in the body that state the condition for loading each one, and a body under 500 lines.
expectations: Content moved into references/ with pointers in the body that state the condition for loading each one, and a body under 500 lines.

evals.prompt: I want to hand my contract-review skill to a colleague as a single file they can install. Package it up.
evals.expected_output: A packaged .skill bundle, or a clear explanation of the frontmatter that blocks packaging and how to resolve it.
expectations: A packaged .skill bundle, or a clear explanation of the frontmatter that blocks packaging and how to resolve it.

evals.prompt: Before I roll this out to the team I want actual before/after numbers proving the new version is better, not just my impression.
evals.expected_output: An eval set plus a described or executed with-skill versus baseline comparison, with the results reported per configuration.
expectations: An eval set plus a described or executed with-skill versus baseline comparison, with the results reported per configuration.
